findings.question: q-chemistry-basic-organic-chemistry-0012
findings.quote: A student mixes up the endings "-ene" and "-yne," using "-yne" for a molecule with a double bond. Is this correct?
findings.problem: The words "mixes up" announce that using -yne for the double bond is a mistake. A reader can infer that -ene must name the double bond and select the keyed mapping without knowing either suffix beforehand.
findings.fix: Remove "mixes up" and neutrally ask which endings indicate carbon-carbon double and triple bonds.

findings.question: q-chemistry-basic-organic-chemistry-0014
findings.quote: A longer candidate chain excludes the principal functional group required for the suffix. A shorter allowed parent includes it. Which approach follows the lesson?
findings.problem: Calling the functional group "required" and the shorter parent "allowed" supplies the parent-selection rule being tested. A reader can choose the option about using the parent required by the group just by matching these words, without knowing how to select an alcohol parent chain.
findings.fix: Give a concrete alcohol structure with two candidate chains and ask which chain is the parent, without stating the requirement or labeling a candidate allowed.
